finding.question: Did Nancy Pelosi say the quoted words about US employers cutting employees’ hours, and what was the context of her remarks?
finding.summary: No firsthand source for the claimed wording was found. The earliest located repetition is a December 2013 blog post that attributes it to Pelosi without identifying an original interview or transcript. In a September 2013 CNN interview, Pelosi was asked about union concerns that the Affordable Care Act could undermine the 40-hour workweek; her recorded response described the law as a liberation allowing people to follow their passions, not the claimed statement that employers cutting hours is good. In an earlier 2012 remark, she described people choosing to change jobs or become self-employed without losing access to health care.

sources.title: Pelosi to Crowley: Hillary more prepared to be President than Obama was
sources.snippet: CROWLEY: Let me ask you then about Obamacare, itself. Coming up for a big date on Obamacare October 1st when people can begin to sign up through the — marketplaces. Do you have any reservations at all? Are you worried at all? And I ask you this because you know union leaders, I mean, James Hoffa is one of those who wrote a letter to you and said Obamacare is now stands would, quote, “destroy the foundation of the 40-hour work week.” That’s pretty tough from a loyal Democratic constituency. PELOSI: Well, we’re working on the issue that relates to all of these multiemployer plans which unions are one and some are charities.

sources.title: Pelosi Calls Republicans 'Anti-Government Ideologues,' 'Legislative Arsonists'
sources.snippet: Pelosi called Obamacare a "liberation" for the American people. "This is life, healthy life, liberty, the freedom to pursue your happiness which could be follow your passion for good rather than follow your palate and be constrained by your policy. It's about wellness. It's about prevention, it's about a healthier America."

sources.title: Pelosi: Obamacare Allows You to Quit Your Job and Become 'Whatever'
sources.snippet: “You want to be a photographer or a writer or a musician, whatever -- an artist, you want to be self-employed, if you want to start a business, you want to change jobs, you no longer are prohibited from doing that because you can’t have access to health care

sources.title: According to Glen: Obamacare Shopping... You Can't Buy It Here!
sources.snippet: In other Obamacare news - Nancy Pelosi recently made a comment about people losing hours at work because of Obamacare. "Employers cutting hours is a good thing," Pelosi said. "It then gives that person time to pursue their dreams and passions."

caveats: The December 2013 blog post is the earliest repetition located in these searches, not necessarily the first appearance of the quotation.
The CNN search result exposes the question and the beginning of Pelosi’s response; the contemporaneous CNSNews report supplies the passion-related wording from the same interview.

report_raw.claim: House Speaker Nancy Pelosi said of US employers, “Employers cutting hours is a good thing. It then gives that person time to pursue their dreams and passions.”
report_raw.justification: A December 2013 blog attributes the exact words to Pelosi but provides no original interview or transcript in the supplied excerpt. [S4] A contemporary account quotes her using similar language about following a passion, but not the claimed words about employers cutting hours. [S2] CNN’s available excerpt shows that she was asked about concerns over the 40-hour workweek, but it does not include the full relevant response. [S1] Inference: The evidence does not establish that Pelosi used the exact words, but the partial transcript and related remarks do not conclusively show that she never said them. Pelosi was Democratic leader in September 2013 and became Speaker again in January 2019. [S6][S8]
key_points: The exact quotation appears in a 2013 blog post without an identified original source. [S4]
A contemporary report quotes Pelosi on following one’s passion, but not on employers cutting hours being good. [S2]
Pelosi was Democratic leader during the September 2013 interview and was Speaker again by the 2020 reference date. [S1][S6][S8]
report_raw.counter_argument: A case for Refuted is that the earliest located exact quotation is unsourced and Pelosi’s documented remarks use different wording about health care and pursuing a passion. [S2][S3][S4] That case does not prevail because the supplied interview excerpt is incomplete, and no source definitively rules out a separate occasion on which she used the claimed words. [S1]
evidence_gaps: A complete recording or transcript of the September 2013 interview would allow the relevant passage to be checked directly.
The original source, if any, behind the December 2013 blog’s exact quotation was not identified.
No independent firsthand source was provided establishing that Pelosi used the exact words on another occasion.
